output.subject: Your questions about refinance rate locks
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for getting in touch with us about your refinance. You asked two questions: if you lock a rate today, how long would that lock stay in place, and is there a fee to extend it? You also mentioned that you haven't picked a closing date yet. We understand that makes the length of the lock an important part of your planning.

We want you to have accurate details that fit your situation, so we have passed your questions to our Mortgage Servicing team. They will review what you've asked and respond within 10 business days with information about the lock period and whether any extension fee applies.

If your plans change in the meantime, for example if you settle on a closing date, please reply to this message and let us know. The team can then take that into account when they get back to you.

Thank you again for your questions. We look forward to helping you with your refinance.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: This is a question, not a complaint. Consider answering it directly in this reply instead of deferring it.
If you answer, add the actual rate lock periods and any extension fees. The draft deliberately states neither.
Rate decisions can be time-sensitive. Consider whether a 10-business-day response is too slow and whether a quicker contact, such as a loan officer, is appropriate.
Confirm that Mortgage Servicing is the right team. Refinance rate locks may belong to a lending or origination team instead.
Check whether the customer has an existing mortgage with the bank, which may affect the information they need.
